name: Ancestral eating (raw organ meats)

card.summary: Ancestral eating with raw organ meats is a diet style built on liver and other organs modelled on hunter-gatherer eating, which followers pursue for strength, leanness and general vitality.
card.note: Raw animal foods carry foodborne-illness risks, and liver is very high in vitamin A.

quick.overview:
Ancestral eating is the idea of eating as pre-agricultural humans are believed to have eaten. In looksmaxxing circles the raw organ-meat version centres on liver and other offal, which proponents prize for nutrient density and as a route to muscle, leanness and energy.

Anthropological reviews describe ancestral diets as varied, with plant-animal balances differing by climate and society, so the organ-heavy form is one interpretation among several.
quick.how: Followers eat liver and other organs, often alongside muscle meat, and some eat them raw or take freeze-dried capsules instead.
quick.risks: Raw meat carries bacterial and parasite risks. Liver contains large amounts of preformed vitamin A, which health authorities caution about in excess, especially in pregnancy.

lead: Ancestral eating is a diet philosophy that takes hunter-gatherer eating as a model for modern nutrition. In looksmaxxing communities one branch emphasises raw organ meats, especially liver, for nutrient density and as a basis for training and physique goals.

Reviews of hunter-gatherer diets describe considerable variety: Paleolithic diets likely included both plant and animal foods, with roughly equal balance among modern warm-climate foragers and more meat in cold climates and among fishing or pastoral peoples [1]. Evolutionary-medicine researchers have argued since 1985 for a hunter-gatherer model for health promotion [2].
A looksmax.org thread shared a paper on the human ancestral diet as support for this style of eating [3].

chain: Eat nutrient-dense organs in an ancestral pattern
Claimed support for energy and recovery
angle.text: Followers eat organs for their vitamin and mineral content and as part of a high-protein diet to support training. The appearance benefit is reached through physique and health, as claimed by practitioners.

paras: The raw-organ version of the ancestral diet treats liver and other organs as central foods, often with the argument that humans are genetically adapted to foods of the Paleolithic era [3].

A 2021 review found that humans eat more meat than other apes and that the plant-animal balance among hunter-gatherers varies widely [1]. A 2009 review noted that Paleolithic-style diets showed favourable cardiovascular and diabetes risk-factor changes in some trials, while pointing to possible shortfalls in vitamin D and calcium [4]. A 2023 review described the hunter-gatherer model as long controversial [2].
No studies found on raw organ-meat diets specifically. Broader work on Paleolithic-style diets is reviewed in [4] and [2].

lore.intro: The ancestral framing appears in looksmax.org discussion of hunter-gatherer diet research [3].

claims.claim: Humans are genetically adapted to ancestral foods, so organ-heavy eating suits us best
claims.believers: A looksmax.org poster shared a paper arguing the human genome has changed little since early modern humans [3].
claims.experts: Reviews report wide variation in hunter-gatherer diets and no single ancestral diet [1][2].
